notes: P04 task SACMAT-X07_mutation_ops (PolicyTrace RQ2 mutant families). evaluation/venue2027/sacmat/mutation_ops.py (MUTATION_OPS_VERSION clara.sacmat.mutation-ops-v1) defines five well-defined policy/trace mutation operators over the audited DSL (evaluation/venue2027/sacmat/policy_trace_dsl.py, task X01), each with a stable operator id and a real mutate(trace, event_index) -> mutated_trace core: MUT_REMOVE_REVOKE (revocation omission — deletes the REVOKE event so delegated authority survives replay; verified PERMIT-after-omission against the independent DSL oracle), MUT_SWAP_GRANT_REVOKE (inverted temporal precedence — moves the directly adjacent REVOKE one slot ahead of its GRANT with logical_time just below the grant's, producing the REVOKE_BEFORE_GRANT class while respecting the DSL's strictly ascending order), MUT_EXTEND_DELEGATION_EXPIRY (stale delegation — rewrites the DELEGATE policy_state epoch token base@t<expiry> to expire at the trace's last logical time; refuses absent tokens NO_EXPIRY_TOKEN, non-integer expiries MALFORMED_EXPIRY and non-advancing rewrites NO_EXPIRY_ADVANCE), MUT_CHANGE_POLICY_VERSION (stale-policy epoch — appends the -v2@ marker with the successor's epoch to one non-terminal event's policy_state; refuses terminal targets EVENT_NOT_FOUND and marker stacking STALE_VERSION_MARKER_PRESENT, which doubles as the no-op guard since an unchanged token necessarily already carries the marker) and MUT_DROP_OBLIGATION (audit-obligation drop — downgrades one ACCESS to a redundant same-scope GRANT so no adjudicable request remains and the outcome degenerates to DENY-by-default). MUTATION_REGISTRY maps the five stable ids to the operator functions; apply_operator refuses unknown ids with UNKNOWN_OPERATOR (case-sensitive, no silent default) and apply_all sweeps every registered operator across every (or caller-specified) event index in canonical (operator_id, target index) order, skipping non-applicable targets with stable refusal codes while deduplicating by canonical trace_sha256 — so every emitted mutant provably differs from the original. Structural well-formedness is enforced fail-closed: every mutant must round-trip through the independent, version-pinned parse_policy_trace before it is returned (a mutant the DSL rejects is refused with the underlying reason code, never emitted), and a defensive TRACE_UNCHANGED post-condition blocks byte-identical outputs. All errors are stable reason codes on MutationOpError; outputs (Mutant.to_dict) are JSON-serializable; pure functions — no clock, no randomness, no I/O, deterministic repeat application. Test driver evaluation/venue2027/sacmat/tests/test_mutation_ops.py: 28 tests, all passed — positive: registry completeness (exactly the five contracted operator ids), each operator's exact structural and semantic effect verified against the independent DSL oracle (revoke omission flips DENY/REVOKED_ACTOR_TRANSITIVITY to clean PERMIT; swap yields REVOKE_BEFORE_GRANT; expiry moves to the last logical time; epoch marker rewritten; dropped obligation degenerates to DENY), mutant JSON round-tripping through parse_policy_trace, JSON-serializable Mutant records, apply_all distinctness (no mutant sha equals the original or another mutant), determinism (byte-identical repeat sweeps, canonical operator ordering), explicit event_indices targeting; adversarial: WRONG_EVENT_KIND for kind-mismatched targets (remove/drop/swap), NO_ADJACENT_GRANT_REVOKE_PAIR for non-adjacent swap targets, NO_EXPIRY_TOKEN / MALFORMED_EXPIRY / NO_EXPIRY_ADVANCE for degenerate delegation-expiry rewrites, EVENT_NOT_FOUND for terminal policy-version targets and out-of-range indices across every operator, STALE_VERSION_MARKER_PRESENT for marker stacking (and as the no-op guard, exercised via a forged already-marked token), EMPTY_TRACE for zero-event traces, UNKNOWN_OPERATOR for unregistered and case-mismatched operator ids, and the UNORDERED_TIMESTAMPS tamper harness proving the DSL round-trip gate rejects structurally invalid histories.
